aerospace.level_flight_cl.title: Lift coefficient required for level flight (C_L = 2W/(ρV²S))

variables.name: C_L
variables.desc: lift coefficient required in level flight
variables.label: CL

assumptions: Level (unaccelerated) flight: lift balances weight, so C_L = 2W/(ρV²S). For the force itself see fluid_dynamics.drag_lift.
method_references: L = W at level flight: C_L = 2W/(ρV²S)

aerospace.wing_loading.title: Wing loading (W/S)
assumptions: Gross-weight wing loading; drives stall speed and manoeuvrability.

aerospace.stall_speed.title: Stall speed from maximum lift coefficient
assumptions: Level flight: L = W at C_Lmax; steady, flaps as configured.
method_references: L = W at stall: v_stall = sqrt(2W/(ρSC_Lmax))

aerospace.aspect_ratio.title: Wing aspect ratio
assumptions: Planform aspect ratio; higher AR lowers induced drag.

aerospace.induced_drag.title: Induced drag coefficient and force
assumptions: Elliptical-loading correction via the Oswald factor e (user input ≈ 0.7–0.9); C_Di adds to the parasite drag coefficient.

aerospace.glide_ratio.title: Glide (lift-to-drag) ratio, glide angle and glide distance

variables.name: d
variables.desc: still-air glide distance from a given height

assumptions: Unpowered steady glide at the best (or chosen) L/D; the still-air glide distance is h·(L/D). L/D itself is the glide distance per unit height.
method_references: L/D = C_L/C_D; tan γ = D/L = 1/(L/D); glide distance d = h·(L/D)

aerospace.thrust_to_weight.title: Thrust-to-weight ratio
assumptions: Instantaneous value; > 1 enables a vertical climb.

aerospace.specific_impulse.title: Specific impulse and effective exhaust velocity
assumptions: Steady thrust; g0 = 9.80665 m/s² so I_sp is the thrust per unit weight flow.

aerospace.rocket_equation.title: Rocket mass ratio and propellant fraction
assumptions: Mass bookkeeping for the ideal rocket: R = m0/mf and propellant fraction m_p/m0 = (m0 − mf)/m0 = 1 − 1/R. The resulting velocity change Δv = v_e·ln(R) is kinetics.tsiolkovsky.
method_references: Mass ratio R = m0/mf; propellant fraction = 1 − 1/R (Δv in kinetics.tsiolkovsky)

aerospace.orbital_velocity.title: Circular orbital velocity

variables.name: GM
variables.desc: standard gravitational parameter of the central body

variables.name: r
variables.desc: orbital radius from the centre of the body

assumptions: Circular orbit; r is measured from the body centre (add the body radius to the altitude). GM Earth = 3.986004418e14 m³/s².

aerospace.escape_velocity.title: Escape velocity

variables.name: GM

variables.name: r
variables.desc: radius from the centre of the body

assumptions: Minimum speed for a parabolic escape trajectory from radius r.

aerospace.orbital_period.title: Circular orbital period

variables.name: GM
variables.desc: standard gravitational parameter of the central body

variables.name: r
variables.desc: orbital radius from the centre of the body

assumptions: Kepler's third law for a circular orbit (r = semi-major axis a).

aerospace.geopotential_altitude.title: Geometric altitude ↔ geopotential altitude (H = r0·z/(r0+z))
assumptions: Converts geometric altitude z (the geometric distance above mean sea level) to geopotential altitude H (the US Standard Atmosphere 1976 independent variable, which accounts for the fall-off of gravity with height). H = r0·z/(r0+z) with r0 = 6356766 m; the two differ by < 0.3 % below 86 km.
method_references: Geopotential altitude H = r0·z/(r0 + z) (US Standard Atmosphere 1976 convention)

aerospace.standard_atmosphere.title: Standard atmosphere (ISA / US 1976) properties vs geometric altitude

variables.name: z
variables.desc: geometric altitude above mean sea level

procedure.python:
def _atmosphere(values):
    """ISA / US Standard Atmosphere 1976 temperature, pressure, density and sound speed vs altitude.

    The input is GEOMETRIC altitude z; it is converted to geopotential altitude H = r0·z/(r0 + z) (the
    US 1976 independent variable) before the layer equations are applied.
    """
    z = values['z']
    r0 = values['r0']
    if r0 <= 0:
        raise MechError('r0 (mean Earth radius) must be positive')
    if z < 0:
        raise MechError('z (geometric altitude) must be >= 0')
    H = r0 * z / (r0 + z)                     # geopotential altitude
    if H > 84852.0 + 0.1:  # 86 km geometric converts to 84852.05 m; allow that boundary (verify24f)
        raise MechError('geometric altitude z = %.1f m is above the tabulated US 1976 range: geopotential '
                        'altitude H = r0·z/(r0+z) = %.1f m exceeds 84852 m (≈ 86 km geometric)' % (z, H))
    # Base pressure/temperature at each layer's lower boundary (march up from sea level).
    Pb = [101325.0]
    Tb = [288.15]
    for i in range(len(_ISA_LAYERS) - 1):
        H0, T0, L0 = _ISA_LAYERS[i]
        H1, T1, _ = _ISA_LAYERS[i + 1]
        if L0 == 0.0:
            P1 = Pb[-1] * math.exp(-_G0 * (H1 - H0) / (_R_AIR * T0))
        else:
            P1 = Pb[-1] * (T1 / T0) ** (-_G0 / (_R_AIR * L0))
        Pb.append(P1)
        Tb.append(T1)
    idx = 0
    for i in range(len(_ISA_LAYERS)):
        if H >= _ISA_LAYERS[i][0]:
            idx = i
        else:
            break
    H0, T0, L0 = _ISA_LAYERS[idx]
    if L0 == 0.0:                           # isothermal layer
        T = T0
        P = Pb[idx] * math.exp(-_G0 * (H - H0) / (_R_AIR * T0))
    else:                                   # constant-lapse-rate layer
        T = T0 + L0 * (H - H0)
        P = Pb[idx] * (T / T0) ** (-_G0 / (_R_AIR * L0))
    rho = P / (_R_AIR * T)
    a = math.sqrt(_GAMMA * _R_AIR * T)
    out = {'H': H, 'T': T, 'P': P, 'rho': rho, 'a': a}
    if H >= _ISA_LAYERS[-1][0] - 200.0:
        out['_warnings'] = ['altitude is near the top of the tabulated US 1976 layers '
                            '(H = 84852 m geopotential ≈ 86 km geometric)']
    return out

assumptions: US Standard Atmosphere 1976 layers, valid to 84852 m geopotential (= 86 km geometric): the input is GEOMETRIC altitude z, converted internally to geopotential H = r0·z/(r0+z) (r0 = 6356766 m) before the lapse-rate and isothermal layer equations give T, P; ρ = P/(R·T) with R = R*/M0 = 287.0531 J/(kg·K) (USSA 1976). Speed of sound a = sqrt(1.4·R·T). Values are the ISA mid-latitude mean, not a weather forecast.
method_references: US Standard Atmosphere 1976 layer equations (recalled base temperatures, lapse rates and geopotential-altitude convention)

source.derivation: v = sqrt(3.986e14/6.3781e6) = sqrt(6.24952e7) = 7905.4 m/s (surface circular orbit, first cosmic velocity ≈ 7.9 km/s)
